explanations.text:
●  you hand over an abstraction                          ([the skill](human))
  │     You write the telling first, free text, and
  │     claude writes the code under it.
  │     The root holds the code and your words; the
  │     human/ folder holds the maps to real lines.
  │
  ●  one run makes the project                            ([the run](The run))
  │     Six steps: keep your words untouched, write the
  │     code, register the project, map the detailed
  │     telling, map your words through the gate, report.
  │     The gate strips the pins and compares the rest
  │     to your file character for character.
  │
  ●  the pins tie words to things                            ([the pins](Pins))
  │     A few words may point at a block, at an earlier
  │     entry, or at another file.
  │     The rules: unique words, real targets, no circle,
  │     the detailed entry before the plainer one.
  │
  ●  the telling takes a shape                    ([the shape](The rail shape))
  │     Claude's telling picks its shape from the catalog
  │     beside this skill — the rail by default.
  │     Your abstraction takes no shape at all; it stays
  │     as you wrote it.
  │
  ●  the laws hold afterwards                              ([the rules](Rules))
        Sync runs exactly once per change. A reword of
        your abstraction goes to abstraction.txt first.
        A repair may re-pin your words but never
        change them.
